headline: A maximum-severity GitLab code execution bug and a flaw in npm's Trusted Publishing that exposed more than 1,500 packages put the developer supply chain at the center of the day.

emerging_trends.text: Frontier AI models now do operator work on both sides of the fence: Booz Allen watched them clear all eight attack objectives against an industrial testbed, Meta published safeguards for Muse Wonder agents that prepare insurance claims and write software, and a Sola Security agent re-graded 9,967 high-severity cloud findings and knocked most of them down.
emerging_trends.topic_title: Frontier AI Clears Every Goal in Booz Allen's OT Lab

emerging_trends.text: Attackers keep subverting the machinery that conveys trust: npm's Trusted Publishing let anyone who re-registered an abandoned GitHub repository name push new versions of a maintainer's package, a spy implant rode Ledger signers to buyers through the reseller CryptoBilis, and Bitdefender's Midnight Mimosa arrived preinstalled in the firmware of MediaTek-based Android phones.

Intrusions keep landing physical bills on retailers: attackers drove refrigeration at hundreds of French supermarkets, among them stores run by Les Mousquetaires, up to 50 degrees Celsius through Danfoss controllers and forced staff to dump chilled and frozen stock, while Ahold Delhaize pulled systems offline across the Netherlands and Belgium.
emerging_trends.topic_title: French Supermarket Freezers Driven to 50 Degrees

topics.title: GitLab Patches a 10.0 Regex Compiler Flaw
topics.latest_developments: GitLab's maximum-severity bug now carries an identifier and a mechanism: CVE-2026-97229 is an integer overflow in the CI/CD Regular Expression Compiler, it affects both Community Edition and Enterprise Edition, and an unauthenticated attacker reaches arbitrary code execution on the server through a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration.
topics.summary: Self-managed GitLab instances carry the risk; GitLab.com customers do not. Administrators should apply the patched releases immediately, since the flaw needs no account on the target.

sources.title: GitLab Patches CVSS 10.0 Flaw That Could Let Unauthenticated Users Run Server Code
GitLab admins urged to patch critical RCE flaw (CVE-2026-97229)
GitLab warns of max severity code execution vulnerability

topics.title: French Supermarket Freezers Driven to 50 Degrees
topics.latest_developments: The attack ran hotter than first reported: on the night of October 11, 2026 the attackers warmed refrigerators and freezers at hundreds of French supermarkets to 50 degrees Celsius, retail chains including Les Mousquetaires confirmed the losses, and the entry point was the single Danfoss controller that runs every cooling unit in a store, a device maintenance firms manage remotely.
topics.summary: One remotely managed controller governs all the refrigeration in a store, which turns a single credential into spoiled stock across a chain. Grocery operators should inventory remote access held by refrigeration maintenance contractors and cut any path that reaches controllers from the open internet.

sources.title: Attackers Heat French Supermarket Fridges Up to 50°C by Hijacking Danfoss Controllers
Refrigeration Controller Hack Spoils Food Across European Supermarkets
Cyberattacks hit European grocers: French supermarket freezers hijacked, Dutch and Belgian stores disrupted

topics.title: Circuit Board Under the Ledger Screen
topics.latest_developments: SecurityWeek described the implant's construction on October 13, 2026: a small circuit board sat hidden under the screens of the Ledger signers, read user data, and transmitted it to the attackers, who drained roughly $86 million from wallets created on devices the Southeast Asian reseller CryptoBilis sold.
topics.summary: Ledger, the Paris-based hardware wallet maker, has paused sales through CryptoBilis and ties every confirmed theft to a device from that reseller. Anyone holding a Ledger signer bought through a third-party reseller should verify the device and move funds to a seed generated on hardware bought direct.

sources.title: $86 Million Crypto Heist Linked to Ledger Signer Hardware Implant
Ledger confirms spy chip implant behind wallet crypto thefts
Ledger Finds Unauthorized Hardware Implant in CryptoBilis-Sold Wallet Amid Fund Theft Reports

topics.title: npm Trusted Publishing Opened 1,500 Packages
topics.latest_developments: Bloom Security disclosed on October 13, 2026 that npm's Trusted Publishing feature let an attacker publish new versions of another maintainer's package by registering a GitHub repository name the maintainer had abandoned, with no stolen credential anywhere in the chain; Bloom counted more than 1,500 exposed packages carrying over 10 million downloads in total, and GitHub, which owns npm, says it has shipped fixes.
topics.summary: Trusted Publishing ties publish rights to a GitHub repository instead of a token, so a renamed or deleted repository leaves the claim open to whoever registers that name next. Maintainers should audit the repositories their npm packages trust and reclaim any name they have retired.

sources.title: npm Trusted Publishing flaw exposed 1,500+ npm packages to takeover

topics.title: Frontier AI Clears Every Goal in Booz Allen's OT Lab
topics.latest_developments: Booz Allen reported on October 13, 2026 that frontier AI models it set against an isolated industrial control testbed in its Chantilly, Virginia lab met all eight attack objectives the firm had defined: the models mapped the network, matched equipment to known weaknesses, wrote working exploits, pivoted into the systems that run production, and in the final test found a robotic arm, took administrative control, and moved it.
topics.summary: The test puts a measured floor under claims that general-purpose models can run operational technology intrusions end to end, against the very equipment that moves physical things. Plant operators should assume exploit development against their known-vulnerable gear now costs an attacker hours instead of weeks and prioritize segmentation between business networks and production control.

sources.title: Frontier AI cleared every OT attack goal Booz Allen set in its lab

topics.title: MarkLogic Flaws Hand Managers the Server
topics.latest_developments: Progress Software published 31 vulnerabilities in MarkLogic Server on October 12, 2026 and rated five of them critical; two let an account holding only partial management privileges seize administrator control of the database server and keep it.
topics.summary: MarkLogic runs enterprise document and search workloads, so an escalation from delegated manager to full administrator exposes everything the database holds. Progress has shipped fixes since September 10, 2026 in MarkLogic 11.3.7 and 12.1.0, and administrators should upgrade and review who holds delegated management rights.

sources.title: Two Critical MarkLogic Flaws Could Give Delegated Managers Persistent Admin Control

business_politics.title: The AI Trade Cracks Again
business_politics.latest_developments: Broadcom's chief executive called the artificial intelligence spending race a "casino," and chip stocks slid worldwide Tuesday, October 13, with Nasdaq futures falling sharply.
business_politics.summary: Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix dropped hard enough to drag South Korea's Kospi sharply lower, and Asian and European technology shares followed as investors questioned the scale of AI capital spending and the pace of Chinese competition. Treasury yields eased partly because money left those shares, which ties the bond market's relief to the equity market's doubt.

sources.title: Chip stocks slide in wake of ‘casino’ comment by Broadcom boss
Nasdaq Futures Fall as Global AI Selloff Intensifies
Asia Stocks Battered as Semiconductor Stocks Dive

business_politics.title: European Gas Reaches a Four-Year High
business_politics.latest_developments: European natural gas prices climbed Tuesday, October 13, to their highest level since December 2022.
business_politics.summary: Escalating attacks in the Middle East threaten Persian Gulf liquefied natural gas cargoes just as European storage sits unusually low for the season, and the standoff between Washington and Kyiv over Russian diesel supplies compounds the squeeze. A global scramble for LNG raises industrial and household energy costs across the continent through the winter.

sources.title: Europe Heads Into Winter With Low Gas Reserves, Uncertain Gulf Supplies
European Gas Prices at Highest Since Late 2022 on Winter Supply Concerns
European gas hits Iran wartime high

business_politics.title: Bond Stress Shifts to the Short End
business_politics.latest_developments: The 10-year Treasury yield fell 5.5 basis points to 5.189% Tuesday, October 13, well below last week's 24-year high, while the Financial Times reported that rising Treasury bill issuance now pressures short-term lending rates and the International Monetary Fund sounded an alarm over governments' public finances.
business_politics.summary: Lower oil prices and the pullback in AI shares pulled Treasury and eurozone yields down ahead of United States inflation data, and record inflows into government bond funds show investors locking in the highest borrowing costs in decades. Strain migrating from the long end to money markets complicates the Federal Reserve's control of short-term rates.

sources.title: Treasury, Eurozone Yields Fall as Markets Look to U.S. Inflation Data
Rising Treasury bill issuance puts pressure on short-term rates
Investors brave US Treasury rout to lock in highest yields in decades
FirstFT: IMF sounds alarm on dire public finances

business_politics.title: JPMorgan Misses as Trading Revenue Falls
business_politics.latest_developments: JPMorgan Chase reported third-quarter earnings below expectations Tuesday, October 13, on falling bond trading revenue, and its shares dropped; Wells Fargo's revenue also disappointed.
business_politics.summary: The two results open a bank earnings season in which Wall Street expects its weakest trading quarter of the year, following a record second quarter built on volatility. Fixed-income desks carried much of the industry's recent profit growth, so a reversal there reshapes revenue guidance across the largest United States banks.

sources.title: JPMorgan earnings miss expectations as bond trading revenues fall
Bank Earnings Roll In: JPMorgan Stock Falls After Profit Misses Expectations

business.title: Dining Out Gets Expensive on Both Sides of the Table
business.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reported Tuesday, October 13, that Pittsburgh restaurant owners describe profitability as down quite a bit while customers absorb higher menu prices.
business.summary: Rising food, labor, and occupancy costs have narrowed margins across Pittsburgh restaurants, and operators tell the Post-Gazette they pass only part of the increase to diners. The squeeze bears on one of the region's larger employers of hourly workers.

sources.title: 'Profitability is down quite a bit': Patrons to restaurateurs, everyone is feeling the cost of dining out

business.title: Verizon Retires Its Copper Lines
business.latest_developments: Verizon told TribLive on Tuesday, October 13, that its copper landline phaseout will not disconnect customers.
business.summary: Michele Vanetta, who has lived in Jeannette her whole life and kept the same number for nearly 40 years at her current house, is among the Westmoreland County customers whose service moves off copper. Verizon says it will carry those lines onto replacement technology rather than cut them.

sources.title: Phone home: Copper landline phaseouts won’t disconnect customers, Verizon says

business.title: Shorty's, Apteka, and Northside Sandwich Week
business.latest_developments: Pittsburgh City Paper's weekly food column, published Tuesday, October 13, carries updates on Shorty's Social Kitchen, New Amsterdam, Apteka, Northside Sandwich Week, and a new Sheetz meat line.
business.summary: The column tracks openings, menu changes, and fall cocktail programs across Pittsburgh restaurants and bars, with Northside Sandwich Week giving North Side shops a week of promotion. Readers get the week's operating news on independent kitchens in one place.

sources.title: Sheetz meatz, North Side sandwiches, fall cocktails, and more Pittsburgh food news

around_town.title: A Voter Guide to 17 Legislative Races
around_town.latest_developments: PublicSource published its 2026 voter guide Tuesday, October 13, three weeks before the November 3 election.
around_town.summary: The guide covers 17 contested legislative races in Allegheny County and prints candidates' answers on Immigration and Customs Enforcement activity, the war, and data center development, the issues readers flagged. Those three subjects have driven the fall campaign across Western Pennsylvania.

sources.title: Voter guide 2026: Where candidates stand on ICE, war and data centers

around_town.title: Rachel Carson EcoVillage Shows Progress
around_town.latest_developments: TribLive reported Tuesday, October 13, that work has resumed at the Rachel Carson EcoVillage site in McCandless after roughly a year of inactivity.
around_town.summary: Backers of the cohousing community, planned around shared space and low-energy construction in McCandless, say obstacles left the property largely undeveloped for about a year and the project still moves forward. The site sits in one of the North Hills municipalities fielding the most new residential proposals.

sources.title: After lengthy delay, signs of progress appear at Rachel Carson EcoVillage site in McCandless

around_town.title: Warm Tuesday, Then Two Impact Days
around_town.latest_developments: WTAE's Tuesday morning update, October 13, keeps the day warm and breezy and tags Wednesday, October 14, an Impact Day for rain, with a second Impact Day behind it.
around_town.summary: Pittsburgh starts Tuesday under patchy fog and mist before afternoon sun, and rain arrives with the next front Wednesday. Temperatures drop sharply through the week behind the system.

sources.title: Warm & Breezy Today; Impact Day with Rain Wednesday
Pittsburgh: Much warmer ahead of two Impact Days

events.title: Joe Manganiello Publishes "Bloodlines"
events.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette reviewed Joe Manganiello's memoir "Bloodlines" on Tuesday, October 13, and ran a companion interview the same day.
events.summary: The Mount Lebanon native and actor opens the book at death's door and closes it in Pittsburgh, where he grew up; the interview covers the Dungeons & Dragons work he calls his dream job. The Post-Gazette treats the memoir as a Pittsburgh story first.

sources.title: Review: Joe Manganiello’s new memoir starts at death's door and ends where he began, in Pittsburgh

events.title: McCandless Holds Its First Restaurant Week
events.latest_developments: WPXI reported Tuesday, October 13, that McCandless's first-ever Restaurant Week is underway.
events.summary: Restaurants across McCandless, the North Hills municipality along McKnight Road, are taking part in the community's inaugural Restaurant Week promotion. WPXI gave no closing date or participant list.

sources.title: Community’s first-ever ‘Restaurant Week’ kicks off in McCandless

around_teams.title: McCarthy Turns to Tampa Bay
around_teams.latest_developments: The Steelers posted head coach Mike McCarthy's Monday, October 12, news conference previewing Week 6 at the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, set for Sunday, October 18, at 1 p.m. Eastern on CBS.
around_teams.summary: Linebackers Nick Herbig and Patrick Queen and guard Mason McCormick took the podium the same day on the team's YouTube channel. The Buccaneers trip follows a four-game stretch that has cost Pittsburgh receivers and defensive backs to injury.

sources.title: Coach McCarthy Press Conference (Week 6 at Tampa Bay Buccaneers) | Pittsburgh Steelers

around_teams.title: The WPIAL's NFL Pipeline Thins
around_teams.latest_developments: The Post-Gazette published an examination Tuesday, October 13, of why the WPIAL and the Pittsburgh City League send fewer players to the NFL than they did a decade ago.
around_teams.summary: Western Pennsylvania high school football long supplied a steady stream of professional players, and the paper traces the decline through participation numbers, recruiting patterns, and the migration of talent to other regions. The trend matters to a city that built part of its identity on that pipeline.

sources.title: The WPIAL is sending fewer players to the NFL than it did a decade ago. Why?

around_teams.title: SNR Drive Takes a Victory Monday
around_teams.latest_developments: Matt Williamson and Wes Uhler spent Monday's SNR Drive, October 12, on the Steelers' Week 5 win over the Indianapolis Colts, with Rob King, the voice of the Steelers, calling in.
around_teams.summary: The team-produced show worked through the game, the rest of the Week 5 NFL slate, and a segment the hosts labeled "winning is better than losing." The hosts note their opinions belong to them rather than the franchise.

sources.title: Recapping The Steelers 34-22 Victory Against The Colts | SNR Drive (Oct.12) | Pittsburgh Steelers
